Shrewd

SHROOD -- one syllable, rhymes with 'brewed.' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Shrewd is intelligent, clever, and perceptive.

The shrewd farmer sold his hay early, guessing correctly that prices would fall after the rains.

Worked Example

Two museums want the same famous painting on loan. The smaller museum's director does her homework and discovers the owner's real worry is security -- so instead of offering more money, she offers a state-of-the-art vault and wins the loan.

The director is shrewd: intelligent, clever, and perceptive about how things and people really work. Shrewd judgment reads the situation beneath the surface and turns that reading into practical advantage.

How Shrewd Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

canny

canny: clever and careful, especially in practical matters

calculating

calculating: coolly working out what will serve one's interests

sharp

sharp: quick to notice and understand

Antonyms

foolish

foolish: showing a lack of good sense

dim

dim: slow to understand

How Strong Is It? — sharp → shrewd → calculating

sharp vs. shrewd

sharp vs. shrewd: Sharp says the mind is quick, while shrewd adds worldly wisdom: a sharp student solves the puzzle fast, but a shrewd one also notices why the puzzle was assigned.

calculating vs. shrewd

calculating vs. shrewd: Calculating is the strongest and coldest: a shrewd trader reads people and situations to everyone's benefit, but a calculating one weighs every kindness for what it will earn.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — shrew

Root — shrew: a wicked or cunning person (Middle English shrewe, named for the shrew, the sharp-biting little animal)

Suffix — -d

Suffix — -d: having the nature of (the Middle English ending -ed, worn down to just -d in this word)

Put it together

Put it together: Shrewd began as Middle English shrewed: shrew (a wicked, sharp-tongued person, named for the sharp-biting little animal) + -d (the -ed ending worn down, 'having the nature of'). Over centuries the wickedness drained away and the sharpness stayed: today shrewd means keenly clever and perceptive, with only a faint memory of its bite.

Use the root in a new word: shrew

Use the root in a new word: shrew: A shrew darted out from under the woodpile, smaller than a mouse and twice as fast.

Word Building

Word Choice

Shrewd praises practical intelligence: a shrewd investor, a shrewd guess, a shrewd judge of character. It sees how the world actually works and acts on it. The praise can cool slightly in context -- a 'shrewd operator' may bend rules -- but on the ISEE, shrewd reads as clever and perceptive, not dishonest.
